title: Web Application
body:
[[HTTP]] is a [[Stateless Protocol]].
**Aside**

---

A program whose interface is delivered over [[HTTP]] and runs in a browser, as opposed to one
installed on the machine. The user visits a [[URL]] instead of running an executable, and the
program is delivered fresh on every visit.

That delivery model is the entire reason this course exists as a subject rather than as a
chapter of software engineering. It buys three things, and costs three:

| You get | You pay |
|---|---|
| no installation, and every user on the current version | every interaction is a network round trip |
| one codebase for every operating system | the [[Client]] is untrusted and inspectable |
| the data lives on the server, so it is shared and backed up | [[HTTP]] is stateless, so continuity has to be rebuilt each request |

The last row is the one the aside above is pointing at. Because the server remembers nothing
between requests, an application that needs to know *who is asking* has to be told again every
time, by something the browser sends along. That is [[Cookies]], and it is why a protocol
detail ends up shaping how the whole application is written.

Structurally, a web application is a [[Client]] half ([[HTML]], [[CSS]], [[JavaScript]]
manipulating the [[DOM]]) talking to a [[Server Side]] half ([[Node.js]] and [[Express]],
backed by [[MongoDB]]) across an [[API]] boundary. Assembled from four named pieces, that is
the [[MERN Stack]]. See [[Frontend]] and [[Backend]] for the same split framed for interviews.
